The manifest defines a preinstall lifecycle script that runs "node exploit.js" during installation. Install-time scripts can execute arbitrary code on the maintainer's or user's machine; the script name "exploit.js" and the absence of repository/author/metadata make malicious intent highly likely. Even without the exploit.js contents, a preinstall hook invoking a local script is a clear, high-risk indicator of deliberate malicious behavior.

The script deliberately executes a shell command via child_process.exec that collects sensitive system information (whoami, hostname, id, current directory, root filesystem listing, /etc/hosts, /etc/resolv.conf) and POSTs it to an external webhook (webhook.site). This is active data exfiltration to a remote host (C2-like behavior) using shell interpolation and suppressed output, which is clearly malicious.
